questions.question_text: Which of the following electrolyte abnormalities is a rare but dangerous side effect associated with citalopram therapy?
questions.explanation: SSRIs therapy has been associated with hyponatremia. The incidence with SSRIs ranges from 0.5% to 32%. Elderly patients are more prone to SSRI-induced hyponatremia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding rivastigmine?

options.text: Concomitant anticholinergic agents can reduce rivastigmine efficacy
Following a break in therapy, retitration is recommended
It is an irreversible cholinesterase inhibitor
Gastrointestinal (GI) side effects with the transdermal formulation are lower compared with the oral formulation
The efficacy of the drug may diminish over time as the disease process advances

correct_answer.text: It is an irreversible cholinesterase inhibitor

correct_answers.text: It is an irreversible cholinesterase inhibitor

questions.explanation: Rivastigmine is a reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor approved for the treatment of Alzheimer disease.

questions.question_text: Bupropion's action on dopaminergic neurotransmission is associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Bupropion is associated with multiple side effects, including psychosis and agitation.

questions.question_text: What is the recommended serum range for lithium during the maintenance phase of bipolar disorder in elderly patients to minimize the risk for drug toxicity?
questions.explanation: Elderly patients often require lower lithium dosages to achieve therapeutic serum levels. A serum lithium level between 0.4 and 0.8 mEq per L is considered safe and therapeutic.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not recommended for the treatment of sundowning?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are ineffective and can worsen symptoms of sundowning.

questions.question_text: Which of the following side effects associated with trazodone limits its usefulness in the management of behavioral problems in the geriatric population?
questions.explanation: Trazodone causes orthostatic hypotension, cardiac arrhythmias, and has sedative properties, which may be more pronounced in elderly patients.

questions.question_text: All of the following physiologic changes in the elderly alter drug pharmacokinetics and increase the susceptibility to adverse effects of medications EXCEPT?
questions.explanation: Increased splanchnic blood flow does not contribute to increased susceptibility to adverse drug effects in elderly.

questions.question_text: Which of the following acts as an antagonist at N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) subtype of glutamate receptor?
questions.explanation: Topiramate, dextromethorphan, amantadine, and memantine have antagonistic properties at NMDA receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding memantine?

options.text: Combination therapy with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors does not offer added benefit
No dose adjustments are required in renal or hepatic insufficiency
It is U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved for mild cognitive impairment (MCI)

questions.explanation: Memantine minimally inhibits cytochrome P450 enzymes and dose reduction is recommended in renal insufficiency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following herbal medication/micronutrients should alert you to the risk of bleeding when coadministered with SSRI?
questions.explanation: There have been reports of spontaneous bleeding associated with G. biloba, which is heightened when used with SSRIs.

questions.question_text: All of the following are potential side effects with donepezil therapy EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea are common side effects of donepezil, but GI bleeding is not typically associated.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the safety of methylphenidate in the geriatric population is true?

options.text: Increased risk of bleeding when coadministered with warfarin

questions.explanation: Methylphenidate may exacerbate tics, can cause anorexia, and is associated with an increase in blood pressure.

questions.question_text: Methylphenidate is useful in the treatment of all the following geriatric conditions EXCEPT:

options.text: Depressive symptoms in medically ill patients
Augmentation of SSRIs in late-life depression

questions.explanation: There are no significant data to support the use of methylphenidate in depression associated with Parkinson disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following steps would have the greatest likelihood of minimizing the drug-drug interaction and ensuring therapeutic drug levels?

options.text: Prescribe the usual starting dose of alprazolam
Prescribe a lower than usual starting dose of alprazolam
Decrease the dosage of his protease inhibitor and prescribe the usual starting dose of alprazolam
Prescribe a higher than usual starting dose of alprazolam
Increase the dosage of his protease inhibitor and prescribe the usual starting dose of alprazolam

correct_answer.text: Prescribe a lower than usual starting dose of alprazolam

correct_answers.text: Prescribe a lower than usual starting dose of alprazolam

questions.explanation: Alprazolam concentrations may be increased by protease inhibitors, necessitating dosage reductions to prevent oversedation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following strategies is least beneficial in ensuring appropriate use of antipsychotics among nursing home patients with dementia-related behavioral problems?

options.text: Attempting dose reduction following stabilization of disruptive behavior
Ruling out preventable causes of disruptive behavior
Close monitoring of antipsychotic adverse effects
Carefully documenting specific behaviors warranting antipsychotics
Utilizing antipsychotics PRN orders instead of scheduled orders

correct_answer.text: Utilizing antipsychotics PRN orders instead of scheduled orders

correct_answers.text: Utilizing antipsychotics PRN orders instead of scheduled orders

questions.explanation: PRN use of antipsychotics is discouraged except in certain situations and should generally be avoided.

questions.question_text: The HELP found that lower rates of delirium were achieved in comparison with standard care when all the following risk factors were addressed EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Antipsychotics have no role in the prevention of delirium.

questions.question_text: Long-acting benzodiazepines can increase the risk of which of the following side effects in the elderly?
questions.explanation: Long half-life benzodiazepines are associated with increased risks of sedation, cognitive impairment, and falls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the use of venlafaxine among the elderly?

options.text: Venlafaxine can be used as a first-line agent for the treatment of MDD
Venlafaxine has significant drug-drug interactions with commonly used medications in elderly
At moderate to higher doses, it inhibits the reuptake of serotonin
Higher dosages of venlafaxine are needed to treat pain syndromes

correct_answer.text: Higher dosages of venlafaxine are needed to treat pain syndromes

correct_answers.text: Higher dosages of venlafaxine are needed to treat pain syndromes

questions.explanation: Venlafaxine at higher doses is needed to treat pain syndromes due to its interaction with adrenergic receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the statements is true regarding trazodone?

options.text: It is a potent blocker of presynaptic α2-adrenergic receptors
Its active metabolite, m-chlorophenylpiperazine (m-CPP), is a weak direct 5-Hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) agonist
It is a weak blocker of postsynaptic α2-adrenergic receptors
It is a mixed serotonergic agonist-antagonist

correct_answer.text: It is a mixed serotonergic agonist-antagonist

correct_answers.text: It is a mixed serotonergic agonist-antagonist

questions.explanation: Trazodone is a mixed serotonergic agonist-antagonist, helping in sleep and depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the use of lithium among elderly?

options.text: Lithium is associated with delirium with serum levels as low as 1.5 mEq/L
They require lower dosage than younger patients to produce similar serum lithium levels
Elderly are sensitive to neurologic side effects even at low doses
Lithium levels should be maintained between 1 and 1.2 mEq/L
Aging increases the risk of lithium toxicity

correct_answer.text: Lithium levels should be maintained between 1 and 1.2 mEq/L

correct_answers.text: Lithium levels should be maintained between 1 and 1.2 mEq/L

questions.explanation: Lithium levels should be maintained between 0.4 to 0.8 mEq/L in the elderly.

questions.question_text: SSRIs are shown to be efficacious in the treatment of which of the following symptoms among dementia patients?
questions.explanation: SSRIs may be efficacious in treating a range of behavioral disturbances associated with dementia.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding the use of SSRIs in the elderly?

options.text: It is recommended to start the SSRI at half their maximal efficacious dose
All the SSRIs are given in a single daily dose
Dosage is usually doubled after 3 to 4 weeks
SSRIs should be used cautiously in patients taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

correct_answer.text: SSRIs should be used cautiously in patients taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

correct_answers.text: SSRIs should be used cautiously in patients taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)

questions.explanation: SSRIs may increase bleeding risk when used with NSAIDs.

questions.question_text: In which of the following coexisting conditions, SSRIs are not recommended for active and maintenance treatment of MDD?
questions.explanation: SSRIs are safe and well tolerated among elderly with these conditions.

questions.question_text: Bupropion is used among the elderly for intolerance to SSRIs. Which of the following side effects would prompt switching to bupropion?
questions.explanation: Bupropion may be used when side effects such as nausea, sexual side effects, severe fatigue, or diarrhea arise from SSRIs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding Mirtazapine?

options.text: It is a presynaptic α2-receptor agonist
Not associated with cognitive side effects
Not associated with hematologic adverse effects
Anti-nausea property is because of its inhibition at the 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors

correct_answer.text: Anti-nausea property is because of its inhibition at the 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors

correct_answers.text: Anti-nausea property is because of its inhibition at the 5-HT2 and 5-HT3 receptors

questions.explanation: Mirtazapine's anti-nausea properties are due to its action on 5-HT receptors.

questions.question_text: SSRIs should be used with caution in which of the following elderly patients?
questions.explanation: Caution is required as SSRIs can interact with these medications and conditions, increasing the risk of bleeding and other complications.

questions.question_text: Mirtazapine is used among the elderly for intolerance to SSRIs. Which of the following side effects would prompt switching to mirtazapine?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine is considered when patients experience side effects such as nausea, sexual side effects, or insomnia from SSRIs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true regarding the use of secondary amines tricyclic antidepressant (TCA) among the elderly?

options.text: Secondary amines are not preferred because of their higher propensity to cause orthostasis and falls
Secondary amines are preferred because of their linear pharmacokinetics
Secondary amines are not preferred because of their anticholinergic effects
TCAs are the first-line drugs in the treatment of late-life depression

correct_answer.text: Secondary amines are preferred because of their linear pharmacokinetics

correct_answers.text: Secondary amines are preferred because of their linear pharmacokinetics

questions.explanation: Secondary amines are preferred in elderly due to their linear pharmacokinetics and lower propensity for orthostasis.

questions.question_text: Venlafaxine is known to cause which of the following cardiovascular side effects among the elderly?
questions.explanation: Venlafaxine can lead to various cardiovascular side effects, including dose-dependent hypertension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cholinesterase inhibitors is not FDA approved for the treatment of Alzheimer disease?
questions.explanation: Tacrine, donepezil, rivastigmine, and galantamine are all FDA approved for Alzheimer disease treatment.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is not true regarding the antipsychotics use for the treatment of psychotic symptoms of any etiology in late life?

options.text: Olanzapine and risperidone have fewer severe extrapyramidal symptoms when compared with promazine and haloperidol
Olanzapine causes more weight gain compared with risperidone
Olanzapine is superior to promazine, haloperidol, and risperidone in efficacy and tolerability
Atypical antipsychotics have become first-line drugs

correct_answer.text: Olanzapine is superior to promazine, haloperidol, and risperidone in efficacy and tolerability

correct_answers.text: Olanzapine is superior to promazine, haloperidol, and risperidone in efficacy and tolerability

questions.explanation: Olanzapine is not proven to be superior to promazine, haloperidol, and risperidone in efficacy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cholinesterase inhibitors is not FDA approved for the treatment of Alzheimer disease?
questions.explanation: All listed medications are FDA approved for Alzheimer's treatment, except tacrine is rarely used due to hepatotoxicity.

questions.question_text: Valproic acid is used among the elderly with bipolar disorder who respond poorly to lithium. Which of the following symptoms would prompt switching to valproic acid?
questions.explanation: All these symptoms may respond well to valproic acid treatment.

questions.question_text: Older patients taking carbamazepine are at higher risk for developing which of the following?
questions.explanation: Carbamazepine can cause various significant side effects, especially in older patients.

questions.question_text: Which would be a reasonable treatment choice for a 72-year-old man with Parkinson disease showing depressive symptoms?
questions.explanation: Recent studies indicate that pramipexole is efficacious in relieving depressive symptoms in Parkinson disease.

questions.question_text: Atypical antipsychotics increase the risk of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics are associated with an increased risk of numerous adverse outcomes including metabolic and cardiovascular risks.

questions.question_text: What should be the next best step after nausea and vomiting occurs with rivastigmine at an increased dose?

options.text: Continue the same dose (3 mg twice a day) and reevaluate in a week
Prescribe promethazine while maintaining the dose of rivastigmine at 3 mg twice a day
Change the dosing schedule to 1.5 mg twice a day
Discontinue treatment for several doses and then restart at a lower dose

correct_answer.text: Discontinue treatment for several doses and then restart at a lower dose

correct_answers.text: Discontinue treatment for several doses and then restart at a lower dose

questions.explanation: The higher incidence of nausea and vomiting with rivastigmine leads to a recommendation of discontinuation and restarting at a lower dose.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cholinesterase inhibitors is not recommended for a patient with end-stage renal disease?
questions.explanation: Rivastigmine's metabolism is affected by renal function, thus it is not recommended for patients with renal insufficiency.

questions.question_text: Which of the following classes of medications is efficacious and safe in the management of chronic agitation associated with dementia?
questions.explanation: SSRIs are found to be safe and efficacious in managing chronic agitation in dementia patients.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding the management of dementia?

options.text: Rivastigmine is FDA approved for mild to moderate Alzheimer disease
Memantine is FDA approved for moderate to severe Alzheimer disease
Donepezil is FDA approved for mild, moderate, and severe Alzheimer disease
Galantamine is FDA approved for mild to moderate Alzheimer disease

questions.explanation: All listed medications have FDA approval for treating various stages of Alzheimer disease.

questions.question_text: Despite a half-life of 1 hour, the cholinesterase inhibitor rivastigmine is dosed twice a day. Which of the following statements is the best explanation for this?

options.text: Rivastigmine remains bound to cholinesterase, thus remaining therapeutically active for 10 hours
Rivastigmine remains bound at the nicotinic receptor site, thus remaining therapeutically active for 10 hours
More frequent dosing of rivastigmine can cause intolerable GI side effects
Frequent dosing helps to control the behavioral disturbances

correct_answer.text: Rivastigmine remains bound to cholinesterase, thus remaining therapeutically active for 10 hours

correct_answers.text: Rivastigmine remains bound to cholinesterase, thus remaining therapeutically active for 10 hours

questions.explanation: Rivastigmine remains bound to cholinesterase and thus stays therapeutically active longer than its half-life would suggest.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding the treatment of Parkinson disease dementia (PDD)?

options.text: Anticholinergic medication are the treatment of choice
Clozapine is FDA approved for behavioral disturbances associated with PDD
Treat with the maximum tolerated dose of dopamine agonist
Rivastigmine is the only FDA-approved treatment for PDD

correct_answer.text: Rivastigmine is the only FDA-approved treatment for PDD

correct_answers.text: Rivastigmine is the only FDA-approved treatment for PDD

questions.explanation: Rivastigmine is the only medication approved specifically for treating PDD.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true regarding coadministration of SSRI with warfarin?

options.text: Fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, and paroxetine appear to have the highest potential for CYP2C9 inhibition
SSRIs increase the risk of bleeding by altering platelet aggregation, and the risk of bleeding may be further increased when combined with warfarin
Competitive inhibition of CYP2C9 could result in potentiation of warfarin-induced anticoagulation when coadministered with SSRI
Increase in prothrombin time is reported with fluvoxamine and fluoxetine when combined with warfarin

questions.explanation: All statements regarding SSRIs' interaction with warfarin and their effects on bleeding risk are accurate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following cholinesterase inhibitors is rarely used in view of its several side effects, mainly hepatic toxicity?
questions.explanation: Tacrine has significant side effects including hepatic toxicity, limiting its use.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the outcomes of the National Institutes of Health (NIH)-funded Clinical Antipsychotic Trial of Intervention Effectiveness study for Alzheimer Disease (CATIE-AD) is/are true?

options.text: CATIE-AD results indicate that patients may benefit symptomatically from treatment with atypical antipsychotics; however, the medications had little effect on measures of functional abilities, quality of life, or care-giving time needed
There were no significant differences on measures of effectiveness between the atypical antipsychotics and placebo
One of the advantages of the CATIE-AD trial is that it included outpatients in usual care settings
In CATIE-AD, atypical antipsychotics were associated with worsening cognitive functioning compared with placebo

questions.explanation: All statements regarding the CATIE-AD study outcomes are accurate.

questions.question_text: Antipsychotics use among the elderly has a black box warning for increased risk of mortality from which of the following?
questions.explanation: The increase in mortality risk primarily arises from cardiovascular causes among the elderly treated with antipsychotics.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true of the rivastigmine transdermal system (Exelon Patch) EXCEPT:

options.text: Dose increases should occur only after a minimum of 2 weeks at the previous dose
A patient who is on a total daily dose of 6 to 12 mg of oral rivastigmine may be directly switched to Exelon Patch 9.5 mg per 24 hours
Dose increases should occur only after the previous dose was well tolerated
The patch should be changed every 24 hours

correct_answer.text: Dose increases should occur only after a minimum of 2 weeks at the previous dose

correct_answers.text: Dose increases should occur only after a minimum of 2 weeks at the previous dose

questions.explanation: Dose increases for rivastigmine transdermal patches should only occur after a minimum of 4 weeks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following would be an appropriate treatment for an 80-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia and prominent apathy?
questions.explanation: Methylphenidate has good evidence in managing apathy in dementia patients.
